The history of computing is a story of abstraction layered upon abstraction. Early engineers wired programs by hand, later generations wrote assembly, and today most developers rarely think about the instructions their code becomes. Each layer hides complexity, but every layer also leaks a little, and the best engineers learn to look beneath the surface when performance or correctness demands it.
